before_msg_a.description: Two invitations with the same invitation id (0x49 repeated) and lookup and different secrets (codes K7QM-2XPA-9RTE and K7QM-ZZZZ-0000), host draws listed in `codes`. Joiner a connects on connection 1 with the same draws. Everything on the wire up to and including AUTHORIZED {join_only, I} (`out`) is the same for both; the first msg_a differs.

conventions.draws: `draws` lists each party's random values in the order it takes them; a `bytes` draw fills a request of exactly that length. Host: the invitation id (16), the code (12; drawn again while its lookup is another open invitation's), then for each new attempt, after the debit and before reading its first message, its CPace scalar yb (32). Joiner: for each attempt the attempt id (16) and its CPace scalar ya (32).
conventions.exporters: On connection n both ends see the pair exporter n + 100 repeated 32 times.
conventions.joiners: Each joiner's identity secret is one byte repeated 32 times: 0x50 for the first joiner a sequence names, 0x51 for the second, and so on. Its JOIN_DIRECT name is its letter. `host` means the host's own identity key.
conventions.limits: The defaults: 600 s lifetime, 5 attempts, a 300 s Allow window, a 1000 ms miss hold.

description: The host side of Pair with IP (wire.md 10.9) with the real code exchange, behind the host's gate (wire.md 8.1). Each sequence starts with one invitation created at `conventions.time`; each step runs one operation, then its expectations hold. Every message from a joiner passes the host's gate first: let through, it reaches the host machine; otherwise `out` lists the gate's verdict (`gate`: ignore) or the host's close. Ops: dial (a new connection from the joiner: step 2 runs with the gate; a provisional or live grant binds it and the host sends AUTHORIZED {live}), connect (dial unless the connection exists, then the joiner sends JOIN_DIRECT {lookup, name}; `lookup` wrong means another lookup), recover (the same with receipt I and, with `cancel`, the cancel flag), submit (the joiner runs one attempt with the right or a wrong secret: it draws an attempt id and its scalar, sends msg_a, checks msg_b; on a failed check it sends CODE_ABORT {A, pairing_failed} and closes with pairing_failed; otherwise it sends msg_c, unless `lose` is msg_c, when the connection breaks first, or `hold` is msg_c, when msg_c stays on its way), deliver (the held msg_c arrives, unless its connection has closed: then `undelivered`), inject (the joiner sends CODE_EXCHANGE with `attempt` and `payload`), cancel (the joiner sends CODE_ABORT {its last attempt, cancelled}, `lost` with `abort` lost, and closes with cancelled, or breaks the connection with `goaway` lost), drop (conn breaks with no GOAWAY), stream (the joiner opens a stream on conn: the gate's verdict, and on commit the host commits the provisional grant before the frame goes on), allow and decline (the owner answers the joiner's request, allow with `role` when given; `result` ok or the refusal), owner_cancel, tick (the host's timer), old_grant (the joiner already holds an owner grant named "<joiner> (old)" made by a ticket pairing whose invitation id has the bytes of I), restart (the host restarts: invitations are gone, the grant table, provisional grants included, is restored, and every connection is gone), abort (the joiner sends CODE_ABORT with `attempt` and `code`). A sequence with `grant_expires_at` (seconds after `conventions.time`) creates its invitation with that grant expiry. tick runs the host's timer for the invitations and then the grant table's expiry (committed grants, then provisional ones, each in grant id order; each expired grant's connections close in one grant_closes with grant_revoked). A failed commit reports the grant's other connections' grant_closes first, then the host's close of the connection whose frame asked for it; a cancel reports the other connections' grant_closes, then enrollment_undone, then the cancelling connection's close. A miss hold holds the connection's gate: until the I/O layer closes it, only keepalive, HELLO and GOAWAY pass. On committed, every gate in `bound` drops its provisional state and the cancel exception; the frame that asked for the commit then passes the gate. A joiner's close is listed, and reaches the host, only when the connection is still up. A wrong lookup is `0000` (`0001` if that is the invitation's), a wrong secret `00000000` (`00000001` if that is the code's). `at` sets the time, in seconds after `conventions.time`, before the op. Expectations: `host_status` (`gone` once the host has forgotten the invitation), `host_attempts_left`, `closed` (connections the host closed during the step with a close of its own, with the code, sorted by connection; connections a grant-table change closes are in `grant_closes` instead, listed only when there are any), `held` (JOIN_DIRECTs answered by a miss hold: the I/O layer holds the connection for hold_ms, then closes it with invitation_invalid; that close is not listed), `requests` (answerable requests: joiner, presence, decision), `grants` (every grant in the table: joiner, name, role, and provisional, direct for a committed grant a direct invitation made, or ticket), `paired` (the PAIRED messages the host sent during the step: connection, role). `out` lists in order every control message each side sent (except the two HELLOs), closes, and what the host told its I/O layer and UI: admitted (join-only gate), miss_hold, attempts_left (after each debit; the code stays the same), approval (the prompt, sent again with the same id when its presence or decision changes), approval_ended, enrolled (a provisional grant, with the grant table's id, counting from 0), bound (a recovery connection bound to a direct grant), committed, enrollment_undone, invitation_ended and grant_closes (grant-table events).

sequences.description: The lookup finds the invitation, the code passes and the owner is asked. Allow makes a provisional grant with receipt I bound to the connection and sends PAIRED. The first stream frame there commits it.
sequences.name: success_with_allow

sequences.description: The right lookup with a wrong secret: the attempt is debited and fails at the joiner, which aborts and closes (one attempt per connection). The code stays the same; the next Connect with it passes.
sequences.name: wrong_secret

sequences.description: A lookup that finds nothing is held, then closed with invitation_invalid by the I/O layer. Nothing is debited, and a device that already holds a grant gets the same answer.
sequences.name: wrong_lookup_is_not_debited

sequences.description: Decline closes the device's connection with pairing_declined and ends the invitation. Its recovery hears pairing_declined until the Allow window ends; then, and for anyone else, there is no open invitation.
sequences.name: decline

sequences.description: Five wrong secrets on five connections. The fifth failure ends the invitation; afterwards the lookup finds nothing.
sequences.name: exhausted

sequences.description: a passes; b then uses up the other four attempts. The invitation stays open while a's request is inside its Allow window: a new attempt closes with attempts_exhausted, and Allow still enrolls a.
sequences.name: a_waiting_request_keeps_an_invitation_without_attempts

sequences.description: The device's connection drops after the code passed; its request stays, away. Allow, with the role viewer, marks it allowed and ends every other request. Its recovery connection is answered AUTHORIZED {join_only, I}, enrolled with that role and sent PAIRED; its first stream frame commits the grant.
sequences.name: allow_while_away_then_recovery

sequences.description: A recovery while the request still waits: AUTHORIZED {join_only, I}, and the same request now points at the new connection.
sequences.name: recovery_while_waiting_for_allow

sequences.description: A device whose connection dropped types the code again on a new Connect: its request (same id) points at the new connection; no second request.
sequences.name: the_same_identity_passing_again_keeps_its_request

sequences.description: Connected, the device cancels: CODE_ABORT {A, cancelled}, then its close with cancelled. The request goes; the invitation stays open. Its recovery hears cancelled until the window ends.
sequences.name: joiner_cancel_while_waiting

sequences.description: The device's connection dropped while it waited; it delivers its cancel on its next connection. The request goes and the connection closes with cancelled.
sequences.name: joiner_cancel_while_away

sequences.description: Allowed while away, the device comes back only to cancel: nothing is granted, and the invitation ends.
sequences.name: joiner_cancel_after_allow_while_away

sequences.description: The owner allows while the device's cancel is on its way. Its CODE_ABORT {A, cancelled} for the attempt that passed goes through the live gate of the connection the host just enrolled; the provisional grant is removed and the host closes with cancelled. The device's own GOAWAY is lost.
sequences.name: cancel_crossing_allow_goaway_lost

sequences.description: As before, but the CODE_ABORT is lost and only the device's close with cancelled reaches the host: that removes the provisional grant too.
sequences.name: cancel_crossing_allow_abort_lost

sequences.description: Once a stream frame committed the grant, the device's CODE_ABORT is ignored by the live gate and its close with cancelled is an ordinary close. A recovery that cancels is answered PAIRED: the grant stays.
sequences.name: a_cancel_after_the_commit_is_too_late

sequences.description: The owner allowed; the connection broke before the device saw PAIRED, and the device cancelled meanwhile. Step 2 binds its next connections to the provisional grant (AUTHORIZED {live}); its recovery carries the cancel, which removes that grant. The other connection bound to it closes with grant_revoked before the host reports the removal.
sequences.name: cancel_by_recovery_after_allow

sequences.description: The owner allowed; PAIRED was lost with the connection. Step 2 binds the recovery to the provisional grant (AUTHORIZED {live}), and the host answers PAIRED from its receipt. The first stream frame commits it.
sequences.name: lost_paired_answered_by_receipt

sequences.description: The pairing connection closes before any stream. The device's next ordinary connection is bound to the provisional grant by step 2 (AUTHORIZED {live}); its first stream frame commits it.
sequences.name: the_first_ordinary_connection_commits

sequences.description: The device's recovery connection ran step 2 before the owner allowed on the original connection, so step 2 bound nothing and sent nothing. When its JOIN_DIRECT arrives, the host binds it to the provisional grant and sends AUTHORIZED {live} before PAIRED.
sequences.name: a_recovery_bound_after_a_late_allow

sequences.description: a already holds a grant (from a ticket whose invitation id has the same bytes as I) and pairs again on connection 2. Allow, with the role viewer, makes a provisional grant: the old grant stays, and connection 1, live under it, opens a stream without committing anything. The cancel crossing Allow removes only the provisional grant; the old one and connection 1 stay.
sequences.name: a_re_pair_cancelled_across_allow_keeps_the_old_grant

sequences.description: As before, but the device takes PAIRED and opens a stream on connection 2: the provisional grant commits, replaces the old grant, and connection 1, bound to the old one, closes with grant_revoked.
sequences.name: a_re_pair_commit_replaces_the_old_grant

sequences.description: a holds a grant from a ticket whose invitation id has the same bytes as I. A direct recovery with that receipt neither removes it (with the cancel flag) nor is answered PAIRED (without): a never passed this invitation's code, so the second recovery hears not_received.
sequences.name: a_ticket_receipt_never_answers_a_direct_recovery

sequences.description: Two devices pass the code, each with its own request. Allowing b with the role viewer enrolls b with its own name and that role, ends a's request and closes its connection with invitation_invalid.
sequences.name: two_identities_pass

sequences.description: The code passes one second before the invitation expires. At expiry the lookup finds nothing, but the request stays answerable for its whole Allow window, past the expiry.
sequences.name: code_passed_in_the_last_second

sequences.description: A connection admitted before expiry starts no attempt at or after it.
sequences.name: no_attempt_at_expiry

sequences.description: An unanswered request ends when its Allow window does, and its connection closes with invitation_invalid. The invitation, not yet expired, stays open.
sequences.name: allow_window_ends

sequences.description: At the end of the Allow window, before the host's timer has run, the request can no longer be allowed or declined.
sequences.name: answers_at_the_window_end_before_the_timer

sequences.description: Allowed while away, the device recovers at the end of the Allow window, before the host's timer has run: nothing is enrolled and the recovery gets the miss hold.
sequences.name: a_claim_at_the_window_end_before_the_timer

sequences.description: The connection drops after the device verified the host's confirmation but before its own reached the host. Its recovery hears AUTHORIZED {join_only, I, not_received}.
sequences.name: recovery_not_received

sequences.description: The device passed the code and cancelled; its outcome is kept until its Allow window ends. A recovery after that, while the invitation is still open, gets the miss hold, never not_received.
sequences.name: a_forgotten_outcome_is_never_not_received

sequences.description: The device's confirmation (msg_c) is still on its way on connection 1 when its recovery with the cancel flag arrives. The host retires connection 1 and its attempt before it answers cancelled, so the confirmation, which then never arrives, opens no request.
sequences.name: a_recovery_cancel_before_the_confirmation_arrives

sequences.description: a passes and goes away; b uses up the other four attempts, so only a's request keeps the invitation open. a's recovery cancels: the invitation ends at once, the next lookup gets the miss hold, and a's next recovery still hears cancelled.
sequences.name: a_recovery_cancel_ends_an_exhausted_invitation

sequences.description: The owner allowed and the connection broke before any stream; then the host restarted. The invitation is gone, but the provisional grant was stored: step 2 binds the recovery to it, the receipt answers PAIRED, and the first stream frame commits it.
sequences.name: a_provisional_grant_survives_a_restart

sequences.description: The device's next connection commits the grant while the enrolled connection is still up. Every connection bound to the grant learns of the commit, so the enrolled connection's gate now ignores the late CODE_ABORT of the attempt that passed, and the grant stays.
sequences.name: a_commit_elsewhere_ends_the_cancel_exception

sequences.description: The device cancelled once and its outcome is kept; it types the code again and its confirmation is still on its way when its recovery cancels. The host retires that connection before it answers with the kept outcome, so the confirmation opens no request.
sequences.name: a_recovery_cancel_with_a_kept_outcome_still_retires

sequences.description: A CODE_ABORT with cancelled that names an attempt other than the one that passed on the connection ends nothing: the request stays.
sequences.name: an_abort_for_another_attempt_keeps_the_request

sequences.description: The device holds a provisional grant; its next connection is bound to it by step 2, then sends a lookup that finds nothing. While the host holds that connection, its stream frame is ignored and commits nothing.
sequences.name: a_held_connection_commits_nothing

sequences.description: a passes at 0 and b at 100; c uses up the last attempts. At 310 a's request is past its window but the timer has not run. b's recovery cancels: no request inside its window is left, so the invitation ends as exhausted and the next lookup gets the miss hold.
sequences.name: an_expired_request_does_not_keep_an_exhausted_invitation

sequences.description: The invitation's grants expire at 100. Allowed while away at 50, the device recovers at 100: the grant would be born expired, so nothing is sent but the close, the invitation ends as invalid, and nothing is granted.
sequences.name: a_claim_after_the_grant_expiry_sends_nothing

sequences.description: An Allow at the grant expiry is refused and changes nothing.
sequences.name: allow_after_the_grant_expiry_is_refused

sequences.description: Allowed at 50, the device opens its first stream at 100: the commit fails, the provisional grant is removed and the connection closes with grant_revoked.
sequences.name: a_commit_after_the_grant_expiry_fails

sequences.description: Allowed at 50; the device's next connection is bound to the provisional grant at 60. At 100 the enrolled connection's first stream frame finds the grant expired: the other connection closes with grant_revoked, then the enrolled one.
sequences.name: a_failed_commit_with_another_bound_connection

sequences.description: Allowed at 50, the device opens no stream; at 100 the timer removes the provisional grant and closes its connection with grant_revoked.
sequences.name: a_provisional_grant_expires

sequences.description: The grant committed at 10; at 100 the timer removes it and closes its connection with grant_revoked, after which nothing on that connection passes the gate.
sequences.name: a_committed_grant_expires

sequences.description: A second attempt on a connection closes it with protocol_error and is not debited.
sequences.name: one_attempt_per_connection

sequences.description: A JOIN_DIRECT from the host's own identity key closes with not_authorized: a device never pairs with itself.
sequences.name: own_identity

sequences.description: The owner cancels while a device waits: its request ends, its connection closes with cancelled and its recovery finds no open invitation.
sequences.name: owner_cancels
